title: Comprehensive Fair Meta-learned Recommender System

problem.claim: Recommender systems face a cold-start problem because fresh users have very limited interaction data.

gap.claim: Fairness issues in meta-learning-based recommender systems are largely overlooked despite their success in improving cold-start recommendation performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Fresh users provide very limited interaction data, creating a cold-start challenge for recommender systems.
Meta-optimization methods learn user preferences from a few past interaction items by learning shared parameters and adapting them to individual users.
Existing recommender systems are vulnerable to bias and unfairness, while fairness in meta-learning approaches has received limited attention.

source_observation.claim: Meta-learning uses shared prior knowledge and limited user-specific training data to address cold-start recommendation.

interpretation.claim: A shared initialization can support rapid adaptation when per-user interaction data is sparse.

application.claim: When applying meta-learning to recommendation, evaluate fairness alongside cold-start performance.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify which fairness definitions, user groups, or evaluation conditions should be used.

unknowns: The proposed method and its specific fairness mechanisms are not described.
No datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions are provided.
The abstract units do not establish explicit author-stated novelty.
